review_method: Read each source record's description, license hint, stars, and updatedAt; performed bounded direct source review for the three stack/dashboard contenders and recorded why each remains held.

candidates.description: Nextjs Boilerplate and Starter with App Router and Page Router support, Tailwind CSS 4 and TypeScript; Next.js 16 + Drizzle ORM + Vitest + Playwright + Storybook
candidates.reason: Direct review confirms MIT, Next 16/React 19, Tailwind 4, Drizzle/Postgres migrations, and Playwright, but the protected routes are generic marketing/counter/auth surfaces rather than a dashboard block; retain as host compatibility evidence, not the feature source.

candidates.description: Shadcn UI NextJS Boilerplate; Free Open-source ChatGPT UI Admin Dashboard Template - Horizon AI Boilerplate
candidates.reason: Direct review confirms MIT, a concrete /dashboard/main route, chart/table components, Next 15/React 19 RC/Tailwind/shadcn, and source SQL; provider-specific Supabase/Stripe wiring plus missing build, smoke, visual, owner, and rollback receipts prevent admission.

candidates.description: Fully featured Next.js / React eCommerce boilerplate with product information and JAMStack edge page generation
candidates.reason: The record establishes a Next/React eCommerce base and MIT hint, but not a read-only dashboard boundary, shared Postgres/ORM contract, or admission proof; the commerce data model would broaden the pilot scope.

candidates.description: Next.js 16+ boilerplate with typescript, husky, lint-staged, biome, vitest, react-testing-library, storybook, and GH actions
candidates.reason: The record reports a current Next.js/test scaffold and MIT hint but no dashboard capability, Postgres/ORM data boundary, or source-level contract receipts.

candidates.description: NextJS 14 starter with TypeScript, Tailwind, Stripe, Mailgun, and Google Auth
candidates.reason: The record reports an older Next 14 stack and provider-specific Stripe/Mailgun/Google Auth side effects; no dashboard boundary or provider-neutral data contract is established.

candidates.description: Jam3 NextJS Generator for SPA, SSG, SSR and JAMStack applications
candidates.reason: The record describes a Next generator and MIT hint but does not identify a dashboard feature, Postgres/ORM boundary, or block-level build/browser/rollback evidence.

candidates.description: Next.js 16.3, TypeScript, React 19, Oxlint, Oxfmt, Tailwind v4, Shadcn, Better-auth, RBAC, i18n, Playwright, Vitest, SEO and PWA
candidates.reason: Direct review confirms MIT, Next 16/React 19/Tailwind 4/Shadcn, Playwright, and a protected admin route, but that route currently renders only a translated header/layout and the package has no identified Postgres/Drizzle data layer; it is a shell/auth fallback, not the read-only feature source.

candidates.description: Front-end boilerplate for building web applications, based on Next.js.
candidates.reason: The record reports only a front-end Next.js boilerplate and MIT hint; dashboard capability, data ownership, token contract, and proof are unspecified.

candidates.description: Fullstack web app starter with Django, django-rest-framework, Next.js and Docker using PostgreSQL as the primary DB
candidates.reason: The record establishes Postgres but introduces a Django/DRF plus Next split and gives no Tailwind/shadcn dashboard boundary or independent block proof; runtime and ownership normalization are material.

candidates.description: Next.js 14 app with user management, permissions, Tailwind CSS, Shadcn UI, Prisma, Postgres, React Table and React Query; description mentions contributions under the MIT License
candidates.reason: The record has strong stated stack fit but reports no machine-recognized license; a description saying contributions are under MIT is not source-level license evidence, so it remains held pending direct review.

candidates.description: An ethereum, next.js, and react.js boilerplate using only open source libraries
candidates.reason: The record reports no license and an Ethereum-specific scope; legal provenance and relevance to a read-only dashboard are both unresolved.

candidates.description: We aim to build the most powerful Next-js Boilerplate so people do not write the same code again
candidates.reason: The record has no license and only a broad positioning statement; there is no content-backed dashboard, data, or proof boundary to assess.
The record has an MIT hint but no description, is the oldest starter in this slice, and does not establish current runtime, dashboard capability, data ownership, or proof.

candidates.description: NextJS 14 credentials/Google/GitHub authentication with PostgreSQL, Prisma, Zod, etc.
candidates.reason: The record reports no license even though the runtime/data shape is relevant; auth is provider-specific and no dashboard route or block proof is identified.

candidates.description: A full featured Next.js boilerplate based on clean architecture, MVVM and functional programming
candidates.reason: The record establishes a recent MIT Next.js architecture starter but not a dashboard surface, Postgres/ORM contract, or independent build/browser/ownership proof.
